title.narrative: Palestinian women and girls lead and engage on Women Peace and Security in oPt

description.narrative: Intermediate Outcome 1: Enhanced prevention and protection of women and girls from violence and human rights violations.

The project centres on structural inequalities and violence against women and girls in the occupiedPalestinian territory (oPt) - a long-standing problem that stems from the protracted Israeli occupation,political division between Palestinian factions and harmful social and patriarchal gender norms thatcontinue to exacerbate marginalisation of and violence against women and girls across the oPt.The problem will be addressed by working through three interlinked pathways of change to achieve threeintermediate outcomes premised on the three Women Peace and Security (WPS) pillars, and Palestiniannational priorities of the WPS agenda at the United Nations and 1325 NAP. Outcome 1 will enhanceprevention of and protection from violence and human rights violations; Outcome 2 will increase themeaningful participation of women, girls and women’s rights organisations (WRO) in decision-makingprocesses at local, national and international levels; Outcome 3 will strengthen accountability for therights of women and girls at national and international levels.

description.narrative: "1.3.1 # of individuals with strengthened capacity (knowledge and skills) to advance women’s rights and gender equality (disaggregated by type, age and gender)MFA Basket indicator 5.2.2"

comment.narrative: Individuals and service providers are still in need of an in-depth understanding of gender equality, equity, women's rights and the relevant existing laws and policies concerning these concepts. In year 1, it was evident through partners’ engagement with the stakeholders of the SGBV referral system that young people and service providers in particular are not aware of the core and essence of family protection law and it applications.

WCLAC designed their interventions to work with grassroots women led organizations, youth led organizations; and service providers of the SGBV referral system, making sure that these target groups have the knowledge and skills needed to advance women’s rights and gender equality.

In 2023, WCLAC continued to support two women led local CBOs in Hebron and Jericho, where they have implemented 20 awareness sessions targeting 302 women on domestic violence, protection from GBV based on the laws implemented in the Palestinian territories, Personal Status law, the importance of adopting the Family protection Bill, the impact of occupation violations on women, and extortion.

WCLAC designed their interventions to work with grassroots youth led organizations; and service providers of the SGBV referral system, making sure that these target groups have the knowledge and skills needed to advance women’s rights and gender equality.

These numbers reflect female individuals who participated in the awareness sessions that were organized by women-led and youth-led CBOs. The sessions mainly focused on GBV and its psychological and social effects on Women, domestic violence, the role of law in protecting women, family protection law, Personal Status Law and polygamy. As for the change, after conducting the sessions 16 women asked for individual social and legal consultations related to their rights (6 social and 10 legal). The post-evaluation showed that the conducted sessions were of great benefit, as women expressed an increase in their knowledge on the aforementioned issues. Furthemore, Al-Muntada colaition) carried out the advocacy campaign that included a 4-day training targeting 48 female students from the faculties of media and law in Palestinian universities in Nablus and Ramallah. The training tackled the following topics: gender-based violence, the family protection law and building interactive activities and initiatives with the aim of raising awareness about the importance of approving the law, and enhancing gender mainstreaming among youth students.

To respond to these findings, projects partners have designed their interventions to work with grassroots youth led organizations; and service providers of the SGBV referral system, making sure that these target groups have the knowledge and skills needed to advance women’s rights and gender equality.

comment.narrative: Palestinian grassroot organizations lack a gendered sensitive dimension within their scope of work. Many organizations are still failing to mainstream or even to recognize gender across their programs and interventions. There is also a need for strengthened cooperation and coordination among partners in terms of advancing gender equality and rights. This need is even more prevalent in youth led organizations.

Projects partners will be working with different actors in the WB and Gaza Strip communities through capacity building and trainings to strengthen their capacity to advance women’s rights and gender equality. These actors were selected according to pre-determined criteria based on their needs, outreach level and capacity to positively influence their communities. The project will aim at uplifting local organizations with a strengthened capacity to advance women’s rights and gender equality.

As for the youth CBO in 2022, WCLAC built the capacity of Sa'er Youth Forum on GBV by providing them with a customized training on applied laws in Palestine as well as Advocating Women's Rights. After the training, Sa'eir Youth Forum implemented 5 awareness sessions where they targeted 80 men in their community, and delivered an innovative initiative where they advocated for women's rights in their local community. WCLAC continued supporting Nibras for Young Generation Society through conducting 5 awareness sessions and targeted 78 men in their local community as well as 1 initiative.

WCLAC partnered with Youth led organization (Nibras) in Bethlehem to build their capacities on themes related to gender justice. Besides the capacity building program, WCLAC hired an expert to work closely with Nibras on developing organization’s strategy and annual plan while ensuring gender mainstreaming. The expert held three intensive meetings with the staff of Nibras with an aim to collect information and analyse the existing situation and develop a strategic plan document that reflects the organization’s interventions with special focus on gender issues.Following the capacity building package, the youth CBO agreed to conduct the following:-a specialized training on gender-based violence, women’s rights and protection mechanisms for 10 members of its board of directors, staff and volunteers.-To develop an action plan that focuses on promoting women’s rights and enhancing CBO's role on genduer justice in the community.-To create a women’s protection committee consisting of 10 members from the association (5 males and 5 females)-To hold annual meetings to monitor the work and identify challenges-To hold awareness workshops on gender-based violence for men in the community

WCLAC continued coordination and cooperation across communities and government by supporting and strengthening the capacities of the three established local protection networks in Hebron, Jericho and Qalqilia. As a result, WCLAC conducted 8 meetings with 3 of the established protection networks attended.The meetings were held to discuss the urgent issues that have been dealt with in the governorates namely, the important role they played by in coordinating efforts between institutions and activating their role, cooperation between the service providers and how to activate their work, and challenges and difficulties they encountered while providing services to women victims of GBV. The discussion during these meetings also revolved around the modified National Referral System, which was adopted by the Palestinian Cabinet; especially the role of service providers and the procedures manual that will govern the implementation of the System.

WCLAC strengthened the capacity of three Protection Networks (Hebron, Jericho and Qalqilya) through supporting them in developing protection plans for the year 2021. Ten coaching and supervision sessions were held; 4 meetings in Hebron (with 20 members;17 females and 3 males), 4 meetings in Jericho (with 12 members;7 females and 5 males) and 2 meetings in Qalqilya (with 15 members; 11 females and 4 males). The sessions aimed to increase service providers' knowledge on the provisions of the family protection law and its relevance to the protection and prevention of violence in the oPt; engage and strengthen the capacity of the members of the protection networks; and increase their knowledge on the role of the state in preventing and protecting women and girls from violence. It is worth noting that the protection networks constitute of representatives from the Ministry of Social Development, the Family Protection Units at the Police, Ministry of Health, Shari’a Judges, the Prosecution Office, Ministry of education and 12 CSO that provide direct services to women victims of SGBV. description.narrative: 1.2.4 # of individuals (female) with strengthened capacity (knowledge and skills) to advance women’s rights and gender equalityMFA Basket indicator 5.2.2

comment.narrative: The number reflects the female individuals from the protection networks who participated in a specialized capacity-building training over two days between October 11th - 12th. The training was designed to unify human rights principles and values that guide the behavior of service providers during intervention and work with battered women, as well as the professional and ethical caveats facing service providers. With the aim to enable the participants to understand concepts of gender and GBV issues in relation to international conventions and frameworks, and to enable the participants to develop provisions of the code of conduct for protection service providers.The training focused on the following themes: Defining gender-based violence, introduction to CEDAW agreement, the standards and principles related to dealing with abused women, right to protection, the content and component of codes of conduct in dealing with GBV victims.

This number reflects the female individuals from the protection networks who participated in two specialized capacity-building training that focused on improving the quality and effectiveness of services provided by the networks’ members. The three-days training program was implemented from the 19th to 21st of December in Nablus Governorate. The second three-days training program was implemented from the 26th to the 28th of December. It aimed to address the challenges faced the protection networks members due to the ongoing political and economic situation in the West-Bank, and focused on crisis management, interpersonal skills, self-motivation and self-care strategies

comment.narrative: Part of WCLAC’s strategy to community engagement is to deliver its services through already established CSOs in the targeted communities. Firstly, this brings more legitimacy to the work when the services comes from CSOs who are based in the targeted communities, brings more localization, and capacitates the aforementioned CSO.

WCLAC aims to establish two MoUs with two CSOs in Hebron and Jericho to deliver legal and psychosocial services. Also, WCLAC will be working to build their capacities in issues related to gender equality and women’s rights.

WCLAC continued its partnership with the two local women led CSOs in Hebron and Jericho, both managed to carry out 20 awareness raising sessions where they targeted 354 (250 females, 104 males) participants. The sessions focused on raising the awareness on cybercrime, GBV prevention, required psychological and social support for women in marginalized areas, responding to crises and emergencies, the challenges facing women and girls in light of political and economic situations and how to overcome these challenges through self-affirmation and awareness. Both CBOs also managed to provide social and legal services to a a total of 150 women victims of GBV. Additionally, WCLAC still has partnership with the General Union for Palestinian Women (GUPW), which is the umbrella of the Personal Status Law Coalition and the National Coalition for implementing UNSCR1325.

This number reflect female individuals who participated in the capacity building training organized by WCLAC on Security Council Resolution No. 1325 related to the agenda of women, peace and security. the capacities of the participants. the capacities of the participants were raised in several topics, including: the international human rights system: the relationship with international humanitarian law and international human rights law, international mechanisms for accountability with focus on Israeli violations of Palestinian women’s human rights (contractual and non-contractual mechanisms and how to utilize them in advocacy), UNSCR1325: the legal obligations of the resolution and the relationship between it and subsequent resolutions, the definition of violence against women in times of war, armed conflict and under occupation within the framework of Resolution 1325 and subsequent UN resolutions, the Palestinian National Plan for UNSCR 1325 and subsequent resolutions, localization of UNSCR1325 with specific focus on the impact on Palestinian women under occupation, Resolution 2250 (Youth, Security and Peace), Recommendation/General Comment No. 30 of the Committee on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women and Resolution 1325 and finally, the importance of advocacy in generating social change. However, according to the post assessment the percentage increased to 90% as after the training they have gained the needed knowledge on advocacy mechanisms, 1325 Resolution, CEDAW and UN mechanisms and the ability differentiate between International Law and Humanitarian Law.

comment.narrative: The oPt legal framework combines various outdated laws derived from the Jordanian law in the West Bank, Egyptian law in the Gaza Strip and other imposed laws from the Israeli occupation. The existing laws in the oPt are yet to be developed to ensure preventative and protection laws are in place and accessible for women and girls. For example, the personal status law and penal code laws have not been revised or ameneded since 1960s. The CSOs in oPt have been advocating towards the enactment of the Family Protection Bill since the PA acceeded to the CEDAW convention in 2014. However, there has been little to no change in the existing discrimantory laws that fail to protect women and girls.

The project aims to maximize the advocacy and lobbying efforts in oPt towards achieving more justice to women and girls through: 1) Enhancing the legal system framework towards enabling the adoption of the family protection law; and 2) Starting a real dialogue and working together platform where CSOs can collaboratively work together towards enhancing enabling legal environment for the enactment of a personal status law that works for women and girls as well. This will be done through national advocacy campaigns, and policy reviews. The employment of both laws will enhave the women, girls and boys protection in oPt.

WCLAC worked diligently to involve the protection centers and female counselors working in the development field. We took all their comments. Additionally, WCLAC worked with the Ministry of Social Development (MOSD) and the Ministry of Women’s Affairs (MOWA) to review and develop the protection mechanisms of shelters system. Currently, WCLAC submitted the semi-final draft for the MOSD and MOWA to be reviewed through their legal units.
